_readme: Product marketing framework (owner, 18 Nov 2026). One file per launch. Matrix 1: what matters most to each user type across ten benefit fields (w: 3 matters most, 2 matters, 1 nice to have) and the claim that resonates. Matrix 2: Series II against Series I. Matrix 3: against Infratech (competitor rule: factual, sourced, needs_approval Specification and compliance). Claims carry no new facts: every fact is in `facts` with its source.
name: Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric Series II

launch.summary: Select and Coastal launched October 2026; Classic follows in January 2027 as Series I sells through. Cobalt is discontinued.

phases.what: Series II Select (Better) and Coastal (Best) launch; Series I moves to entry level; Cobalt discontinued
Series II Classic (Good) launches; Series I discontinued

tiers.name: Tungsten Classic
notes: 2 and 3 kW added to the existing 4 and 6 kW; same voltage options
Black body, stainless steel end covers and metal face guard

tiers.name: Tungsten Select
tiers.colours: Black, white and graphite (graphite on 4 and 6 kW)
tiers.fascia: Diamond Pattern standard; oval and star patterns sold separately

tiers.name: Tungsten Coastal
notes: 316 marine-grade stainless steel for coastal environments
4 and 6 kW only, same voltage options

upgrades: Low-clearance recess kit (Select and Coastal): fits shallow ceilings and tight soffits
Slimmer body: 140 mm (5.5 in) deep and 183 mm (7.2 in) wide, against 156 mm (6.1 in) and 214 mm (8.4 in) for Series I
New accessories: wall-mounting bracket, pitched-ceiling adaptor (3/12 to 12/12), bracket with set positions at 15°, 30° and 45°

aesthetics.claim: Slimmer and sleeker than before, in black, white or graphite: heat that looks as considered as the room it warms.

design_flex.claim: Choose the fascia, the colour and the mount that suit your home, and change the look later with a new fascia.

controls.claim: Turn the warmth up, down or onto a schedule from your phone with Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls.

warranty.claim: Backed by Bromic's manufacturer warranty, so the evenings outside are worry-free.

multi_area.claim: Warm the dining table, the lounge and the pool house as separate zones, each at its own setting.

m2.s1: 2000, 3000, 4000 and 6000 W; coverage published as 65, 100, 130 and 160 ft² (product page; the manual says up to 64, 100, 120 and 144 ft²). Quartz-sheathed steel coil element; 4000 and 6000 W have two elements.
m2.s2: Same four power levels on Select (2–6 kW); Classic adds 2 and 3 kW to its 4 and 6 kW; Coastal is 4 and 6 kW. [[VERIFY: Series II coverage per model and element design — Product team]]
m2.so_what: The warmth customers trust carries straight over: the story is design and fit, with no trade-off in heat.

m2.s1: Wall (straight or 30°), ceiling, chain or 3 ft tube suspension, and recessed.
m2.s2: Adds a sleek single-post mount (Select, Coastal), a new wall-mounting bracket, a pitched-ceiling adaptor for 3/12 to 12/12 roofs, and a bracket with set positions at 15°, 30° and 45°.
m2.so_what: Vaulted porches, gables and angled walls are now standard details rather than custom work.

m2.s1: Included brackets of 6.5 in (2000/3000 W) or 9.5 in (4000/6000 W); recessing needs an installer-built ceiling box in Hardie or cement board.
m2.s2: Classic keeps Series I mounting; one low-clearance recess kit serves Select and Coastal; preset bracket angles. [[VERIFY: what the low-clearance kit includes and fitting time — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Less to fabricate on site and fewer site decisions: quicker to quote and quicker to fit.

m2.s1: Standard recess kit only, which needs a deep ceiling cavity (Bromic guidance: at least 20 in, with two layers of 5/8 in fireproof insulation). No low-clearance option for Tungsten.
m2.s2: New low-clearance recess kit for Select, and a marine-grade low-clearance kit for Coastal, made for shallow ceilings and tight soffits. Classic uses the existing recess kit. [[VERIFY: minimum cavity depth for the low-clearance kits — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Flush Tungsten heat reaches alfrescos, patios and low soffits that were out of reach: a new set of projects to win.

m2.s1: Intertek ETL/cETL listed; IPX4; minimum mounting 72 in on a wall and 96 in on a ceiling (96 in in all cases in Canada); designed for intermittent use.
m2.s2: Electric infrared with no flame or fumes, as before. [[VERIFY: Series II listing, IP rating and minimum mounting heights — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Peace of mind is unchanged; confirm the Series II listings before launch claims use them.

m2.s1: Honeycomb mesh fascia; 2000/3000 W in black, 4000/6000 W in black or white. Body about 214 mm (8.4 in) wide and 156 mm (6.1 in) deep (launch deck).
m2.s2: Slimmer: about 183 mm (7.2 in) wide and 140 mm (5.5 in) deep, roughly 14% narrower and 10% shallower. Diamond Pattern standard on Select and Coastal; Classic in a stylised wireframe with stainless end covers. [[VERIFY: Series I dimensions differ between the deck (214 × 156 mm) and the manual (8.5 × 3.5 in) — Product team]]
m2.so_what: A visibly slimmer, more designed heater: the reason to choose Series II at first glance.

m2.s1: One fascia design; two colours on the larger models.
m2.s2: Three fascia options on Select (Diamond Pattern standard; traditional oval and star sold separately); black, white and graphite (graphite on 4 and 6 kW). Three tiers: Classic, Select, Coastal.
m2.so_what: Designers can match the heater to the room and change the look later, without changing the heater.

m2.s1: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off and Dimmer controllers and the manual wall switch; the two elements on 4000/6000 W can be switched separately.
m2.s2: Same Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls, with the Affinity Dimmer as the recommended controller. [[VERIFY: Series II control compatibility per model — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Nothing new to learn for installers or homeowners: the same app, dimmer and wall switch.

m2.s1: 2 years on the heater, 7 years on the elements; replacement heater or part, owner pays labour and shipping.
m2.s2: [[VERIFY: Series II warranty terms, including Coastal — Product team]] Partners receive an additional year on qualifying products.
m2.so_what: Confirm whether Coastal's marine-grade build earns longer cover: it would be a strong launch message.

m2.s1: Four outputs and mounts for most covered spaces.
m2.s2: The same outputs, plus single post, pitched ceilings, low-clearance recessing and a coastal model, so one family covers more of the spaces on a project.
m2.so_what: One product family for the dining terrace, the vaulted porch and the waterfront deck.

m2.s1: Not rated for marine use: Bromic advises mounting under cover, away from rain, snow and salt mist; stainless grade not published.
m2.s2: Tungsten Coastal in 316 marine-grade stainless steel, with a marine-grade low-clearance recess kit.
m2.so_what: Tungsten can now be sold to coastal homes and waterfront venues, a market Series I could not serve.

m2.s1: 220–240 V, 208 V and 277 V options; rated 8.3 to 25 A at 240 V.
m2.s2: Same voltage options across Classic, Select and Coastal.
m2.so_what: No re-design of circuits: Series II drops into existing electrical plans.

m2.s1: A single range listed at about $798–$1,246 a heater (bromic.com).
m2.s2: Good, Better, Best: Classic $643–$921, Select $923–$1,170, Coastal $1,195–$1,321. Series I moves to entry level and is then discontinued; Cobalt is discontinued. [[VERIFY: launch list prices by model and region — Sales operations]]
m2.so_what: A lower entry price with Classic, and clear steps up for design and coastal performance.

m2.s1: Installation manual, cut sheet, design service and technical support.
m2.s2: The same support, plus new launch literature, photography and training. [[VERIFY: Series II manuals, CAD and Revit files at launch — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Make sure trade files are live on launch day: specifiers will look for them first.

rows.infratech: 1.5 to 6 kW in single and dual element models; the manual gives about 11 ft × 11 ft average coverage for the 6,000 W dual-element model at 8–12 ft.
rows.bromic: 2 to 6 kW; Bromic publishes up to 160 ft² for the 6000 W Tungsten (Series I). Coverage methods differ, so like-for-like claims wait for testing. [[VERIFY: Series II coverage and a like-for-like test against Infratech — Product team]]

RES.claim: Lead with the warmth people feel at the table, not a coverage race.

BLD.claim: Match output to plan size from 2 to 6 kW in one family.

INS.claim: Equivalent outputs; size on Bromic's published coverage and the design plan.

COM.claim: Let the free design plan prove coverage seat by seat.

ARC.claim: Specify by the design plan, model by model.

DES.claim: Talk about where the warmth lands, not the wattage.

rows.infratech: Wall, ceiling, flush, pole and drop pole; flush mounting is for flat ceilings only, and only on the W/WD models.
rows.bromic: Single-post mount, pitched-ceiling adaptor for 3/12 to 12/12 roofs, bracket presets at 15°, 30° and 45°, and recessing.

RES.claim: Vaulted porch or gable? Tungsten mounts neatly to a pitched ceiling with a dedicated adaptor.

BLD.claim: Pitched-ceiling adaptor and single post handle the porches and gables in your plans.

INS.claim: Preset 15°, 30° and 45° positions and a pitched-ceiling adaptor take the guesswork out of angled mounts.

COM.claim: A slim single post suits canopies and pergolas where ceilings are not flat.

ARC.claim: Detail heaters on pitched ceilings and posts with standard Bromic hardware.

DES.claim: Heat follows the architecture, flat ceiling or not.

rows.infratech: Flush frames need a framed pocket of at least 2×8, lined on all five sides with 5/8 in Type X drywall, with the junction box outside the pocket; one dealer quotes 1–2 weeks for flush frames.
rows.bromic: One low-clearance recess kit across Select and Coastal; Classic keeps familiar Series I mounting. [[VERIFY: what the low-clearance kit includes, so the comparison is like for like — Product team]]

RES.claim: Less building work around the heater means a tidier, faster install.

BLD.claim: Fewer framing details to coordinate: one Bromic kit across two tiers.

INS.claim: One kit, familiar mounting and preset brackets: less to fabricate on site.

COM.claim: Shorter fit-outs mean the terrace opens sooner.

ARC.claim: A simpler recess detail to draw and to coordinate.

DES.claim: An easier install keeps the design intact through the build.

rows.infratech: Flush mount needs a 2×8 framed pocket on a flat ceiling; the decorative Motif fascias cannot be used flush or recessed.
rows.bromic: Low-clearance recess kit made for shallow ceilings and tight soffits, with a marine-grade version for Coastal. [[VERIFY: low-clearance kit minimum cavity depth — Product team]]

RES.claim: Shallow patio ceiling? Tungsten can still sit flush.

BLD.claim: Win low-soffit alfrescos without deepening the ceiling.

INS.claim: Fit flush heaters where a 2×8 pocket will not go.

COM.claim: Flush heat in shallow canopies keeps the venue's ceiling clean.

ARC.claim: Flush heat in shallow soffits that other recess frames cannot reach.

DES.claim: A clean ceiling plane even where the cavity is shallow.

rows.infratech: UL/cUL/CE; IPX4; the flush-frame drawing recommends a cool-down after 4 hours of continuous use.
rows.bromic: Electric infrared with no flame or fumes; Tungsten (Series I) is ETL/cETL listed and IPX4. [[VERIFY: Series II listings and IP rating — Product team]]

RES.claim: Safe, clean electric warmth with no flame or fumes.

BLD.claim: Listed, electric and simple to inspect.

INS.claim: Clear mounting heights and listed hardware for a first-time pass.

COM.claim: No flame, no fumes, no cylinders to manage.

ARC.claim: Listed electric heat with published clearances.

DES.claim: Warmth that sits safely beside soft furnishings.

rows.infratech: Bodies about 8.2 in wide and 2.5 in deep (retail listings); 304 stainless as standard.
rows.bromic: Series II is about 7.2 in wide and 5.5 in deep (launch deck), with a rounded profile and Diamond Pattern fascia. [[VERIFY: Series II depth measured the same way as Infratech's 2.5 in body — Product team]]

RES.claim: Lead with the look of the fascia and colours rather than thickness.

BLD.claim: Sell the design and the flush option, where Tungsten leads.

INS.claim: Compare installed depth, including brackets, before quoting slimness.

COM.claim: Lead with the refined fascia and the flush, low-clearance option.

ARC.claim: Use the low-clearance recess, not body depth, as the design argument.

DES.claim: Lead with pattern and finish choices.

rows.infratech: Brushed stainless, 8 standard colours and custom colours; four Motif fascia patterns, on C/CD surface-mount models only.
rows.bromic: Black, white and graphite; Diamond Pattern standard with oval and star options on Select. [[VERIFY: whether Tungsten fascias can be used recessed — Product team]]

RES.claim: Choose the fascia and colour that suit your home, and change the look later.

BLD.claim: Three colours and three fascias cover most model-home palettes.

INS.claim: Fascia changes without re-wiring or re-mounting.

COM.claim: Coordinate finishes across a venue from one family.

ARC.claim: If fascias work recessed, Tungsten offers patterned heaters flush in the ceiling.

DES.claim: Patterns that can work flush in the ceiling, where Motif cannot.

rows.infratech: Switches, timers and panels; Wi-Fi and app control through Bond-powered smart switches, bundled with the Universal Control Panel; integration with Lutron, Crestron, Control4 and Savant.
rows.bromic: Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls: dimming, app, schedules and zones from the controller, Alexa and Google Assistant, and Control4, Crestron or Lutron (compatibility varies); Wi-Fi and app features need compatible Affinity controls, sold separately.

RES.claim: One Bromic app for warmth, schedules and zones, designed with the heater.

BLD.claim: A smart upgrade from one brand, not a third-party add-on.

INS.claim: Commission heater and controls from one manufacturer in one visit.

COM.claim: Zones and schedules from one system, with building integration where needed.

ARC.claim: One manufacturer for heater and control, with BMS and home-automation options.

DES.claim: Dimmable warmth from a single, elegant control system.

rows.infratech: 3 years against defects for the original purchaser at the original site; elite dealers may add a fourth year; competitor controls may void cover; element rated to 5,000 hours.
rows.bromic: Tungsten (Series I): 2 years on the heater and 7 years on the elements; partners receive an additional year on qualifying products. [[VERIFY: Series II warranty, including Coastal — Product team]]

RES.claim: Seven years of cover on the heating elements.

BLD.claim: Partner warranty extension on qualifying products.

INS.claim: One manufacturer stands behind heater and controls.

COM.claim: Long element cover protects the part that works hardest.

ARC.claim: Element cover the client can count on.

DES.claim: Cover that matches the life of the design.

rows.infratech: Solid-state zone and timer panels for multiple heaters.
rows.bromic: Affinity controllers in 1, 2 or 5 channels with app zones, and mounts for every space type in one family.

RES.claim: Warm the dining table and the lounge as separate zones from one app.

BLD.claim: One family covers patio, alfresco and balcony on every plan.

INS.claim: Wire zones on Affinity channels; one controller family.

COM.claim: Run each area only when guests are there.

ARC.claim: One specification family across terraces, balconies and courtyards.

DES.claim: A consistent look across every outdoor room.

rows.infratech: 316 stainless offered as a Marine UpGrade option on C, CD, W and WD models; flush frames listed in 304 stainless.
rows.bromic: Tungsten Coastal is 316 marine-grade stainless as standard, with a marine-grade low-clearance recess kit.

RES.claim: Coastal homes get marine-grade build as standard, recessed or surface-mounted.

BLD.claim: One coastal model, marine-grade by design, for waterfront developments.

INS.claim: Marine-grade heater and marine-grade recess kit for coastal jobs.

COM.claim: Marine-grade from heater to recess kit for waterfront venues.

ARC.claim: Specify a marine-grade recessed heater as a single system.

DES.claim: Coastal finishes that keep their looks by the sea.

rows.bromic: 220–240 V, 208 V and 277 V options; 2 to 6 kW.

BLD.claim: 208 and 240 V cover most residential plans.

INS.claim: Check projects needing 120 V or 480 V early.

ARC.claim: Confirm the supply voltage at design stage.

DES.claim: Works with the supply the space already has.

rows.infratech: Retail about $766 to $1,092 for comparable 4 kW models, including the 316 marine grade (retail snapshots).
rows.bromic: List from $643 (Classic) to $1,321 (Coastal). [[VERIFY: launch list prices by model and region — Sales operations]]

RES.claim: Premium Bromic design from $643 list with Classic.

BLD.claim: Three clear price points from one family.

INS.claim: Offer clients a choice on every quote.

COM.claim: Coastal performance at a defined price step.

ARC.claim: A clear Good, Better, Best for value engineering.

DES.claim: Design-led choices at three price points.

rows.infratech: Trade program with design guides, CAD details and continuing-education credits; elite dealers get leads and training.
rows.bromic: Bromic Partner Program: partner pricing, free custom heating design plans, extended warranty, a dedicated point of contact and project marketing spotlights; CAD and Revit files and AIA-accredited courses.

RES.claim: A free design plan shows where every heater goes.

BLD.claim: Partner pricing, design plans and a dedicated contact.

INS.claim: A dedicated contact and technical line behind every job.

COM.claim: A design plan mapped to every table before you commit.

ARC.claim: Revit files, AIA courses and design plans on request.

DES.claim: Project spotlights that showcase your work.
